thread.title: Fairfax County projects need for up to 95,000 new homes by 2035
thread.title_full: Fairfax County projects need for up to 95,000 new homes by 2035

author: a. j. paul
title: Fairfax County projects need for up to 95,000 new homes by 2035
text:
Fairfax County will need between 41,000 and 95,000 new homes by 2035 to meet housing demand, according to a recent county housing needs assessment presented to the Board of Supervisors on February 10. The projection includes both rental and ownership units.
The assessment found that over the past decade, the growth in housing supply has not matched job growth. From 2013 to 2023, there were 2.13 jobs added for every new home constructed, highlighting an imbalance between employment opportunities and available housing.
There is a significant shortage of affordable rental homes for residents earning up to 60% of the Area Median Income (AMI). Currently, Fairfax County lacks approximately 13,800 rental homes affordable at this income level or below. The report notes that thousands more affordable units will be needed over the next ten years.
The gap in homeownership affordability continues to widen. In 2024, the median home sales price reached $770,000. A family of four would require a household income of at least $230,000 to afford such a home. Additionally, every single-family detached home built in 2025 sold for more than $1.1 million.
Rental affordability remains a challenge for many households in Fairfax County. Almost half (45%) of all renter households are considered cost-burdened because they spend more than 30% of their income on rent and utilities. This figure rises to 87% among renters earning less than $75,000 per year.
According to the Board Matter presented by Board of Supervisors Chairman Jeff McKay: “The data will also inform a housing production roadmap and action plan.”
A video recording of the February 10 meeting is available through the Channel 16 BOS Committee Meetings archive.
